#### List:

- Skeletal muscle physiology
- Length-tension graph and mechanism
- Tension-velocity graph and mechanism

#### Skeletal muscle physiology:

![](/content/exams/anzca/2001/A/2/prize-image001.jpg){fig-alt="Sarcomere structure showing actin, myosin, Z lines and the A, H and I bands"}

- Excitation: action potential at motor nerve terminal → depolarise post-junctional membrane
- Contraction: muscle depolarisation → ↑Ca^2+^ → cross-bridge cycling

#### Length-tension relationship:

![](/content/exams/anzca/2001/A/2/prize-image002.jpg){fig-alt="Skeletal muscle active, passive and total force against percentage resting length"}

- Total tension = active + passive
- Active tension:
  - Actin-myosin cross bridge cycling
  - Usual sarcomere length 1.8μm
  - Optimal sarcomere length 2.2μm sarcomere. Ideal balance between
    - a)↓Length → ↑actin-myosin overlap
    - b)↑Length → ↑TnC affinity for Ca^2+^ → ↑actin exposure by tropomyosin
- Passive tension:
  - Stretch of muscle and connective tissue (some elasticity)

#### Tension-velocity relationship:

![](/content/exams/anzca/2001/A/2/prize-image003.jpg){fig-alt="Force–velocity relationship showing eccentric and concentric muscle contraction"}

- Energy spent on either shortening or force production
- Hence reciprocal
